citations.F1: `serialize_event` does one `fetchrow` per event, so 1,000 events is 1,000 sequential round trips on a single pooled connection. Fix: one `WHERE id = ANY($1)` for the distinct actor IDs
citations.F2: `seen` is a list, so `ev["dedupe_key"] in seen` is O(n²) — ~1.8 M comparisons for acme. Fix: a set.
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` is a synchronous `requests.get` inside an async handler, so up to 1,000 sequential 2 s-timeout HTTP calls block the event loop
citations.F4: there is no index usable by this query ... Fix: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` grows one float per request forever at ~30 req/s per worker ... Fix: bounded ring buffer (or a real histogram)
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` grows one entry per distinct client IP forever. Fix: ... an LRU with a size cap.
citations.F7: Re-measure after each change with the same Datadog p95 for org 4127 and org 88, and separately poll `/healthz` while an acme request is in flight
citations.F9: Do not ship the on-call proposal. Neither half works ... 16 workers × pool max 50 × 6 pods = up to 4,800 Postgres connections
citations.F11: The Redis cache would have a ~0% hit rate: `since` defaults to `datetime.now(timezone.utc) - 30d`, so the cache key is unique per request down to the microsecond.
